hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Live-cell transferrin imaging in both isogenic pairs of human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells showed a lower endosomal pHrodo-transferrin/AF647-transferrin ratio with APOE4 versus APOE3, indicating higher, less acidic endosomal pH, across three independent differentiations with 30 cells per experiment for each pair and a significant overall genotype effect.
rows.Finding quote: We found that ApoE4 iCE-BECs had increased signal for each of the Tf-fluorescent conjugates but a lower fluorescence ratio (Figures 5E and 5F). This result points to a higher uptake of Tf and to a higher endosomal pH (i.e., less acidic) in ApoE4 iCE-BECs.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher endosomal pH in human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells (iCE-BECs), homozygous APOE3 versus APOE4 in two isogenic pairs: Bioni037-A (16423) versus Bioni037-A4 (I40-53), originating from fibroblasts of a healthy APOE3-homozygous individual with the APOE4 line generated by allele editing; and Alstem iPS26 versus iPS16, originating from human bone marrow CD34-positive mononuclear cells with the APOE3 line edited from the parental APOE4 line. Experiments were performed at differentiation day 14 by the general methods default, three days after PECAM1 sorting. Cells were incubated with 25 μg/mL each of pHrodo Red-transferrin and AF647-transferrin for 10 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2; live fluorescence imaging quantified their integrated intensity ratio per endosome.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Measuring pH-sensitive FITC–dextran fluorescence relative to Texas Red–dextran in isogenic human iPSC-derived cortical neurons showed no significant difference in endolysosomal pH between APOE4, APOE3, APOE2 and APOE-null neurons, with three plates and two wells per plate imaged per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Our results show that endolysosomal pH is not changed in any of the APOE isoform-expressing cortical neurons (Fig. 3C,D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in endolysosomal pH in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons differentiated from isogenic EBiSC iPSC lines APOE ε3/ε3 (BIONi010-C-2), APOE ε4/ε4 (BIONi010-C-4), APOE ε2/ε2 (BIONi010-C-6) and APOE-null (BIONi010-C-3). Neurons were loaded with 500 µg/ml FITC–dextran and 250 µg/ml Texas Red–dextran for 24 h, washed and incubated in fresh medium for another 24 h. High-content imaging measured FITC/Texas Red fluorescence ratios within Texas Red-positive cell-body vesicles, averaged per well. Exact neuronal age at assay was not stated.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Human APOE4-expressing astrocytes showed significantly lower LysoTracker fluorescence than APOE3-expressing astrocytes after 30 minutes of staining, suggesting reduced lysosomal acidity (higher pH), although the figure legend inconsistently states that APOE4 lysosomal pH is lower.
rows.Finding quote: Moreover, APOE3-expressing astrocytes showed higher lysosomal activity as indicated by higher lysotracker signal compared to APOE4-expressing cells (Fig. 4D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LysoTracker fluorescence in human astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosomal acidity and higher lysosomal pH)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3- versus APOE4-expressing astrocyte cultures previously described in reference 23; derivation, donor age, and isogenic status are not specified in the supplied text. Cells were incubated with 60 nM LysoTracker Deep Red for 30 minutes at 37 °C, washed, trypsinized, and analyzed for mean fluorescence by FACScan flow cytometry within 30 minutes of resuspension. No additional treatment is stated for Fig. 4D.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: LysoSensor measurements showed that acidic-organellar pH was significantly higher by 0.14 units in immortalized APOE4 versus APOE3 mouse astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: We found that both APOE3 and APOE4 astrocytes had standard lysosomal-related pH, with a minimal but significant difference of 0.14 pH units between genotypes, APOE4 lysosomes being more alkaline (Fig. 4g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher acidic-organellar pH in immortalized mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes from human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, provided by Dr. Holtzman; donor age and strain background not stated for these cultures; passages up to 10; acidic-organellar pH measured with 2 μM LysoSensor Yellow/Blue DND-160 in isotonic solution containing 10% FBS, using calibrated ratiometric fluorometry.

rows.Finding description: Western blotting normalized to β-actin showed higher V-ATPase subunit V0D1 expression in immortalized APOE4 versus APOE3 mouse astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Indeed, the expression of V-ATPase subunit V0D1, which is highly expressed in astrocytes [61], was higher in APOE4 cells than in APOE3 cells (Fig. 4f).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher V-ATPase V0D1 expression in immortalized mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes from human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, provided by Dr. Holtzman; donor age and strain background not stated for these cultures; routinely cultured in advanced DMEM with 10% FBS, passages up to 10; V0D1 protein measured by western blotting and normalized to β-actin.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Ratiometric transferrin measurements in three biological replicates showed approximately 0.84 pH unit lower endosomal pH in mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4 than in those expressing human APOE3.
rows.Finding quote: Endosomal pH in ApoE4 astrocytes was strongly reduced by ∼0.84 pH unit, relative to ApoE3 ( Fig. 3 B ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower endosomal pH in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by David M. Holtzman; donor age, strain background, and primary versus immortalized status were not stated. Cells were serum-starved for 30 minutes, then incubated with FITC-transferrin (75 μg/ml) and Alexa Fluor 633-transferrin (25 μg/ml) at 37°C for 55 minutes. Endosomal pH was measured by calibrated ratiometric flow cytometry of approximately 10,000 cells per sample in biological triplicates.

rows.Finding description: Ratiometric dextran measurements in mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE isoforms showed significantly higher lysosomal pH by >1 pH unit in APOE4 versus APOE3 cells, measured in biological triplicates.
rows.Finding quote: In contrast, we observed >1 pH unit elevation of lysosomal pH in ApoE4 astrocytes ( Fig. 3 C ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal pH in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by David M. Holtzman; donor age and strain background not stated. Baseline genotype comparison using pH-sensitive pHrodo-green-Dextran (5 μg/ml) and pH-insensitive Alexa Fluor 647-Dextran (10 μg/ml), loaded for 12 hours followed by a 6-hour dye-free chase; calibrated ratiometric flow cytometry of approximately 10,000 cells per sample in biological triplicates.

rows.Finding description: Western blotting with densitometric quantification relative to β-actin showed approximately 45% lower NHE6 protein abundance in human APOE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes than in APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: NHE6 protein was concomitantly decreased by ∼45% in ApoE4 astrocytes, compared with ApoE3 ( Fig. 4 C ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower NHE6 protein abundance in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by David M. Holtzman; maintained in DME-F12 with 10% FBS and 200 μg/ml Geneticin/G418 at 37°C and 5% CO2; no additional treatment reported for this comparison; NHE6 Western blotting and densitometric quantification of monomeric and dimeric forms relative to β-actin; mouse age, strain background, and culture duration not stated.

rows.Finding description: Quantitative PCR in mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE isoforms showed approximately 56% lower NHE6 transcript abundance in APOE4 than APOE3 cells, with no significant difference between APOE3 and isogenic APOE-knockout cells, across three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: Although the NHE6 transcript was similar in ApoE KO mouse astrocytes and ApoE KO astrocytes with knock-in of human ApoE3, it was ∼56% reduced in ApoE4 knock-in cells ( SI Appendix , Fig. S5 E ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower NHE6 transcript abundance in mouse astrocytes); (APOE-knockout -> APOE3) -> (no change in NHE6 transcript abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, compared with isogenic ApoE-knockout astrocytes; provided by David M. Holtzman; maintained in DME-F12 with 10% FBS and 200 μg/ml Geneticin/G418 at 37°C and 5% CO2; no additional treatment specified; donor age and culture duration not reported; NHE6 mRNA measured by TaqMan quantitative real-time PCR using the ΔΔCt method.

rows.Finding description: Treating human APOE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes with TSA (5 μM for 12 h) significantly increased endosomal pH compared with DMSO in biological triplicates.
rows.Finding quote: TSA treatment (5 μM for 12 h) exhibited a compartment-specific effect of significantly elevating endosomal pH ( Fig. 5 D ) without effect on lysosomal pH ( SI Appendix , Fig. S8 F ).
rows.Finding summary: (DMSO -> TSA treatment in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (higher endosomal pH)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE4, provided by David M. Holtzman; TSA (5 μM, 12 h) versus DMSO. Endosomal pH measured by calibrated ratiometric flow cytometry using FITC-transferrin and Alexa Fluor 633-transferrin after 55 min uptake at 37°C, analyzing approximately 10,000 cells in biological triplicates. Donor age and mouse genetic background not stated.

rows.Finding description: Wild-type NHE6 expression alkalinized endosomes in human APOE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes. L188P and G383D failed to produce this alkalinization. The endosomal pH assay used biological triplicates.
rows.Finding quote: Like monensin, NHE6 alkalinized the endosomal lumen in ApoE4 astrocytes, but the CS patient mutations did not ( SI Appendix , Fig. S6 H ).
rows.Finding summary: Wild-type NHE6 raised endosomal pH in APOE4 mouse astrocytes. Neither tested variant reproduced that effect.
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic human APOE4 knock-in, supplied by David M. Holtzman; lentiviral expression of GFP-tagged wild-type NHE6, L188P, or G383D, with untransfected and empty-vector controls. Endosomal pH measured by calibrated flow cytometry using pHrodo Red-transferrin and pH-insensitive Alexa Fluor 633-transferrin after 55 minutes at 37°C; approximately 10,000 cells per biological replicate. Donor age, strain background, and interval after transduction not stated.

rows.Finding description: qPCR analysis of mouse astrocytes with human APOE4 versus APOE3 knock-in showed approximately 70% lower NHE9 transcripts (P=2.7×10−5), approximately 67% lower lysosomal V-ATPase V0a1 transcripts (P=9.7×10−5), and no significant difference in plasma-membrane NHE1 transcripts (P=0.946), with n=3 independent experiments; these transcript measurements provide indirect evidence about pH.
rows.Finding quote: There was also an ApoE4-specific reduction in the transcript for the related endosomal isoform NHE9 (∼70% lower) and the lysosomal V-ATPase V0a1 subunit (∼67%), but not for the plasma membrane NHE1 isoform ( SI Appendix , Fig. S5 F ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower NHE9 and lysosomal V-ATPase V0a1 transcripts; no change in plasma-membrane NHE1 transcripts in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by David M. Holtzman; maintained in DME-F12 with 10% FBS and 200 μg/ml Geneticin/G418 at 37°C and 5% CO2; transcript expression measured by TaqMan quantitative real-time PCR using the ΔΔCt method, with three independent experiments; donor age, mouse background, and culture duration not stated.

rows.Finding description: Confocal immunofluorescence showed greater HDAC4 colocalization with nuclear DAPI in human APOE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes than in APOE3 astrocytes (Pearson’s correlation coefficient 0.51 ± 0.02 versus 0.17 ± 0.01; n = 150 per condition), providing indirect mechanistic support for NHE6 repression and endosomal acidification.
rows.Finding quote: Fractional colocalization of HDAC4 with DAPI revealed prominent overlap, consistent with increased nuclear translocation in ApoE4 astrocytes ( Fig. 5 B ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater HDAC4 colocalization with nuclear DAPI in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4, supplied by David M. Holtzman; no additional treatment specified for this comparison; donor age, genetic background and culture duration not stated; anti-HDAC4 immunofluorescence with nuclear DAPI staining, confocal microscopy and Pearson colocalization analysis using the JACoP ImageJ plugin.

rows.Finding description: Monensin treatment (50 μM for 1 h) increased endosomal pH from 5.38 ± 0.01 with vehicle to 5.74 ± 0.03 in human APOE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes (n = 3 biological replicates), providing indirect rescue evidence because treatment changed while APOE genotype remained constant. Group values printed on the figure: Panel E bars labelled 5.38 and 5.74; *** above comparison, but no legend key provided.
rows.Finding quote: Thus, monensin treatment (50 μM for 1 h) elevated endosomal pH in ApoE4 knock-in astrocytes from 5.38 ± 0.01–5.74 ± 0.03, relative to the vehicle-treated control ( Fig. 3 E ), without altering cell viability ( SI Appendix , Fig. S5 A ).
rows.Finding summary: (vehicle -> monensin) -> (higher endosomal pH in APOE4 mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic human APOE4 knock-in, provided by David M. Holtzman; donor age and mouse strain background unspecified; monensin 50 μM for 1 h versus vehicle; calibrated ratiometric endosomal pH measurement by flow cytometry using FITC-transferrin and Alexa Fluor 633-transferrin after 55 min uptake at 37°C, approximately 10,000 cells per sample in biological triplicates.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: LysoSensor measurements showed significantly lower baseline lysosomal pH in E4 than E3 primary mouse microglia, while myelin challenge significantly lowered pH in E3 cells and produced a slight increase in E4 cells with no significant difference from their baseline.
rows.Finding quote: Following treatment with myelin, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes (Figure S3). Interestingly, a similar decrease in lysosomal pH was observed in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia at baseline. As lysosome function is optimal at lower pH, these effects may reflect activation of the lysosomal degradation machinery to cope with the increased burden of internalized debris following myelin challenge in E3 microglia, or in E4 vs E3 microglia even before myelin challenge. E4 microglia did not exhibit further acidification following myelin challenge but rather a slight (albeit not significant) increase of their lysosomal pH (Figure S3).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower baseline lysosomal pH in primary mouse microglia); (myelin challenge) -> (lower lysosomal pH in APOE3 microglia; no change in lysosomal pH in APOE4 microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled forebrains of P1–3 homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on a C57BL/6 background; enriched after approximately 28 days in mixed glial culture and allowed to adhere for 24 hours before experimentation; baseline and myelin-challenged conditions; challenge protocol used 10 μg/ml myelin for 3 hours followed by washout, but the Fig S3 measurement time is unavailable; lysosomal pH assessed using 2 μM LysoSensor Green DND-189 for 10 minutes and flow cytometry of live, DAPI-negative cells.
rows.Data location: Fig S3 (panel mapping unavailable; supplementary panels and legend unavailable)

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Ratiometric OregonGreen measurements across three independent biological and technical replicate experiments showed higher lysosomal pH in human APOE4-expressing murine Neuro-2a cells (pH 5.86) than in APOE3-expressing cells (pH 4.30) or parental cells without human APOE (pH 4.58).
rows.Finding quote: We found that HsAPOE4-expressing cells exhibit dramatic lysosomal alkalinization (pH = 5.86) compared to HsAPOE3 (pH = 4.30) cells (Figure 1C–E), reminiscent of previous results in APOE4-expressing astrocyte lysosomes (pH = 5.20, compared to pH = 4.08 in APOE3 astrocytes) [26]. This alkalinization was also observed in comparison to the parental cell line in which no human APOE had been introduced (referred to as HsAPOE−/−, pH = 4.58).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal pH in murine Neuro-2a cells)
rows.Experimental system: Male murine Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cell lines expressing transgenic full-length human APOE3 or APOE4, compared with parental cells lacking human APOE; endogenous murine Apoe remained intact; passages 5–10. Lysosomal pH was measured by calibrated ratiometric confocal imaging after overnight loading with OregonGreen 488–dextran (70,000 MW) beginning on culture day 3 and a 1-hour chase the following day.

rows.Finding description: Representative LysoTracker images from three distinct biological and technical replicate experiments showed reduced acidic-compartment staining in human APOE4-expressing versus APOE3-expressing mouse Neuro-2a cells, suggesting endolysosomal alkalinization or reduced endolysosomal density rather than directly measuring pH.
rows.Finding quote: We found that the LysoTracker intensity was significantly reduced in HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Figure 1A,B), suggesting either endolysosomal alkalinization or a reduction in endolysosomal density.
rows.Finding summary: (HsAPOE3 -> HsAPOE4) -> (reduced acidic-compartment LysoTracker staining in mouse Neuro-2a cells)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cell lines modified to express full-length human APOE3 or APOE4 from the human APOE locus with flanking genomic regions; endogenous murine Apoe remained intact; passages 5–10. LysoTracker staining on culture day 3, loaded for 30 minutes at 37°C and chased in dye-free culture medium, followed by live-cell confocal microscopy.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, 48-hour TMED5 siRNA knockdown significantly lowered relative lysosomal pH compared with scrambled controls in human APOE4-expressing mouse Neuro-2a cells, alleviating APOE4-associated alkalinization with APOE3 scrambled-control cells shown as a reference.
rows.Finding quote: We confirmed by lysosomal Oregon-green pH measurements that knockdown of TMED5 significantly enhanced lysosomal acidification in HsAPOE4 Neuro-2a cells, while not impacting the lysosomal density (Figure 5C–E).
rows.Finding summary: (TMED5 knockdown vs scrambled control in APOE4 Neuro-2a cells) -> (lower relative lysosomal pH)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells modified to express full-length human APOE4, with endogenous mouse Apoe intact; human APOE3-expressing Neuro-2a cells treated with scrambled siRNA served as a reference. Cells were used at passages 5–10 after 48 hours of Tmed5 or scrambled siRNA treatment. Relative lysosomal pH per lysosome was measured by ratiometric Oregon Green 488–dextran imaging following overnight loading and a 1-hour chase, with pH-clamped calibration.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, LGALS3BP knockdown modestly increased relative lysosomal pH in HsAPOE3 Neuro-2a cells compared with scrambled controls, with scrambled-control HsAPOE4 cells serving as an alkalinized genotype reference.
rows.Finding quote: To assess whether this was driven by changes in lysosomal acidification or the density of lysosomes, we loaded the Neuro-2a cells with Dextran-Oregon Green, finding that LGALS3BP knockdown modestly alkalinized the lysosomal pH, but nearly halved the lysosomal density (Figure 4C–E).
rows.Finding summary: (LGALS3BP knockdown in HsAPOE3 Neuro-2a cells) -> (higher relative lysosomal pH)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells expressing transgenic full-length human APOE3, with endogenous mouse Apoe intact; passages 5–10; 48 h siRNA-mediated Lgals3bp knockdown versus scrambled siRNA, with scrambled-control HsAPOE4 Neuro-2a cells as reference; relative lysosomal pH measured per lysosome by ratiometric Oregon Green 488–dextran confocal imaging after overnight loading and a 1 h chase.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Live-cell imaging of 25–26 DIV primary mouse neurons expressing human APOE (n = 6 embryos) showed significantly lower total somatic LysoTracker intensity with APOE4 than APOE3 (35.6% reported mean difference), an acidity-sensitive surrogate consistent with reduced acidification; pH was not calibrated.
rows.Finding quote: Remarkedly, similar to the DQ BSA results, we detected a 19.8% lower number of LysoTracker positive vesicles (p = 0.011) and a 35.6% lower total LysoTracker intensity per neuronal cell body (p = 0.0059) in ApoE4 compared to ApoE3 neurons (Fig. 4, I–K), supporting the scenario that ApoE4 neurons, after longer time in culture, have lower number of active degradative compartments.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower total somatic LysoTracker intensity in primary mouse neurons, consistent with reduced endolysosomal acidification)
rows.Experimental system: Primary neurons in mixed hippocampal/cortical cultures harvested from embryonic day 15–17 human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, cultured to 25–26 DIV with age-like stress; cultures also contained astrocytes and oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Neurons were identified by synapsin I promoter-driven GFP introduced using lentiviral vectors at 15 DIV. LysoTracker Red DND-99 (1:10,000) and Hoechst were applied for 10–15 minutes before Operetta CLS live-cell imaging; total LysoTracker spot intensity per neuronal cell body was normalized to the sum across all three genotype groups within each experiment. No calibrated luminal pH measurement was reported.
